fixed.explanation: sparsify_labels compares formatted strings, so distinct values that print the same (like large floats shown as 2.015000e+11) get merged. I added an optional `keys` argument to sparsify_labels that is used for the equality comparison. _format_multi now passes the level codes as keys, so only labels that are actually equal are merged.

query.intent: Code that renders a MultiIndex row index in a DataFrame (to_string/HTML/repr) by sparsifying repeated labels. It compares formatted strings of level values instead of the underlying codes, so distinct values that format identically get merged into one group.
query.symptom: Distinct MultiIndex row labels that format to the same string (e.g. large floats shown as 2.015000e+11) are displayed as a single merged/sparsified group.

history.analysis: MultiIndex._format_multi formats each level to strings and then calls sparsify_labels on those strings, so distinct values that format identically get merged. I need to see sparsify_labels and get_level_lengths to decide whether to sparsify using codes instead.
